text: Why is `void process(List<String> items)` better than `void process(ArrayList<String> items)`?
choices: It defers the choice of implementation to run time rather than compile time.
It avoids the cast the JVM would otherwise insert at every call site.
It allows the method to modify the list, which an `ArrayList` parameter would forbid.
It accepts every kind of list, including `List.of` results, and does not let the body depend on anything `List` did not promise.
explanation: On a parameter, take the weakest type that does the job. Demanding `ArrayList` rejects perfectly good lists for no reason, and it invites the body to reach for `ensureCapacity` or `trimToSize`, at which point the restriction becomes real. The rule has limits: on a return type, the weakest type is not always right — returning `Collection` where every caller wants indexing has weakened the contract for no gain.
